notes.summary: The genuine mixed finite-energy operator, mass normalization, necessary target energy and uniqueness hold on singular projective varieties. The exact existence theorem remains conditional on the genuine envelope property.
notes.detailedSummary: Directly reconstructed from BJ1801.08229v4 for reduced irreducible projective varieties over algebraically closed trivially valued characteristic-zero fields and ample real numerical Cartier classes, including ample line bundles. Relative integral closure retains nonnormal generic fibers. The mixed intersection pairing supplies positive Radon measures, raw mass V, probability normalization and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Comparison, domination, integrability and uniqueness precede envelopes. Finite dual energy is equivalent to all-E1 integrability. EP supplies compactness and attainment; surjectivity conversely implies EP.
notes.text:
Source-based partial theorem. Let k be algebraically closed, trivially valued and of characteristic zero, X reduced irreducible projective, and omega an ample real numerical Cartier class, including c1(L) for every ample line bundle. Put V=(omega^n)>0. BJ1801.08229v4 retains singular and nonnormal varieties in Section 7 and general irreducible varieties in Theorem 12.8. Smoothness supplies EP in Theorem 5.20; it is not an unconditional singular conclusion of 12.8.

Relative integral closure of a test configuration is taken in its given generic fiber. Absolute normalization would change that fiber. Theorem 1.13 provides vertical R1/S2 and vertical DVR valuations v_E=b_E^(-1)ord_E, with b_E=ord_E(t). The genuine mixed model measure is sum_E b_E product_i((theta_i,model+D_i)|_E) delta_vE. Relative nefness makes its weights nonnegative; the fiber intersection cycle gives mass (theta_1...theta_n).

The compactified intersection pairing extends by decreasing model majorants, is finite on mixed E1 tuples, and extends multilinearly to differences. Theorem 7.18 defines its Radon measure by integral h M=pairing((0,h),(theta_1,phi_1),...,(theta_n,phi_n)) for PL_R tests. Positivity bounds this functional by its mass times the sup norm; PL density and Radon representation supply existence and uniqueness. Proposition 7.19 gives actual model agreement, mixed integrability, decreasing continuity and normalization pushforward. Weighted and strong continuity follow from 7.21 and the pairing estimates. This constructs the genuine operator independently of equation surjectivity.

E(phi)=pairing((omega,phi)^(n+1))/((n+1)V), E(0)=0 and E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c. Raw diagonal MA has mass V; probability MA=raw/V. Finite energy permits minus-infinity values on pluripolar sets. Model locality and weighted continuity give comparison integral_{phi<psi} MA(psi)<=integral_{phi<psi} MA(phi). With I=integral (phi-psi)(MA(psi)-MA(phi)), Corollaries 10.4/10.6 give uniqueness modulo one constant and genuine global domination without smoothness or EP. Finite-dual-energy divisorial Dirac tests separate normalized potentials through divisorial determination.

For nu of mass V, put mu=nu/V. The exact condition is E_dual(mu)=sup_{psi in E1}(E(psi)-integral psi mu)<infinity, equivalent to integrability of every E1 potential. Necessity for solutions follows from the energy tangent inequality. The converse integrability characterization uses the bounded-J weighted-sum contradiction and I(t phi,0)<=t[1-(1-t)^n]I(phi,0)<=n t^2 I(phi,0), giving -integral phi mu<=A sqrt(J(phi))+B. This characterization does not assert solvability.

With EP, general Theorem 5.11 supplies normalized psh compactness. Strict energy concavity bounds J along maximizing sequences; Proposition 9.19 gives bounded-J L1 convergence against the fixed target, and energy upper semicontinuity gives attainment. Its target approximation precedes attainment by Theorem 9.11. Uniform genuine energy differentiation and the Legendre inequality, tested against f and -f, prove the actual equation. Thus EP gives arbitrary-support finite-dual-energy existence uniquely modulo one constant. Target completeness and the MA bi-Lipschitz embedding give E1 completeness after surjectivity. Conversely, bounded increasing maxima of model competitors are I-Cauchy by the mixed energy formula and produce continuous envelopes. The envelope antecedent is therefore essential.

These are source deductions with explicit antecedents, not mathematical certification by execution.

notes.summary: A noncircular upper-growth smooth affine regularization repair and an explicit affine FS supporting barrier are proved. Their field scope does not cover arbitrary nondiscrete completed residue fields.
notes.detailedSummary: Direct truncation produces a constant boundary neighborhood and local pshness under the actual decreasing tropical-PL definition. Independently reconstructed smooth local-to-global theory uses genuine smooth BJ Dirac solutions, without singular BFJ applications or affine regularization as an antecedent. Global sequences restrict to actual rational affine FS functions with generators and a floor. An entropy barrier supplies strict supports and compact gap sublevels; rational approximation, real-slope truncation, series tails and PL-exhaustion gluing establish its affine FS supporting application under corrected upper growth.
notes.text:
Using n1 and the inspected preceding Wu2609.27610v1 and CLD1204.6277v2 local/model proofs, the smooth affine base is repaired. Use the explicit UPPER convention u<=h+B for actual affine FS h, with local psh defined as generically finite usc decreasing rational tropical-PL limits. Printed Wu Definition 3.15 instead imposes a lower bound. On A1 over Qbar, a=log|z| is the decreasing limit of actual affine FS a_m=max(log|z|,-m) and satisfies the upper bound. Every FS function has a finite floor, whereas a(0)=-infinity, so the printed lower-growth membership fails. Changing that sign alone does not validate Proposition 4.19's invocation of regularizable-input Lemma 3.25.

For smooth affine Y, take a smooth projective compactification with effective ample boundary divisor. Boundary blowups retain such a divisor using m times the pullback minus the effective exceptional divisor, whose negative is relatively ample. Choose rational semipositive theta, boundary section s, and actual FS potential g=-log|s|_theta>=0. Polynomial degree bounds give u<=Ag+B with rational A>0. For rational c>1 and C set phi_C=max(u-cAg,C) on Y, extended as C at the boundary. If B-(c-1)AR<C, then phi_C is identically C on the entire open boundary neighborhood {|s|_theta<exp(-R)}. It is bounded and usc. Since cAg is an actual model potential after clearing denominators, phi_C+cAg=max(u,C+cAg) is locally psh; semipositivity handles the boundary constant.

The independent smooth local-to-global input is reconstructed from the earlier machinery. Continuous PL limits give positive CLD currents, and CLD model positivity gives the nef criterion. Common-neighborhood PL approximants with a strict collar margin glue into genuine global psh functions; different references are accounted for by a global PL shift. This transports BJ mixed measures to the bounded local cone, with mass, locality and comparison. Smooth BJ EP gives continuous genuine divisorial Dirac solutions; perturbation yields local domination. Contact orthogonality and a decreasing net of continuous majorants then give smooth local-to-global pshness. Neither singular Dirac existence nor the disputed affine regularization is assumed.

Consequently phi_C is global psh. Decrease C to minus infinity; generic finiteness follows from a finite point of u. Global decreasing closure and unconditional sequential model/FS regularization apply. Add a complete very ample system with sufficiently low rational weights, leaving each metric unchanged. Its ratios by the distinguished power of s generate k[Y] and provide a rational floor. Hence phi_i+cAg are actual decreasing affine FS functions. The smooth weakly-psh base follows by already-regularizable principal-open extension, smooth tail-supremum EP and divisorial determination. This retains algebraically closed trivial characteristic-zero fields.

For the supporting replacement define chi(t)=a^(-1)log(1+sum exp(-a t_i)) on (R union {infinity})^r, with log(r+1)/a<=1. Then max(0,-t_i)<=chi<=max(0,-t_i)+1. At t put p0=1/Z, pi=exp(-a t_i)/Z and C=-a^(-1)sum pi log pi. The support l_t(t')=C-sum_{pi>0} pi t'_i has nonpositive slopes. Its gap multiplied by a is relative entropy, nonnegative with unique zero at t, including infinity strata. If the gap is <=b, all coordinates are bounded below by -(b+C)/p0, and positive-support coordinates are bounded above using sum pi t'_i<=b+C. Gap sublevels are compact, proving a uniform positive gap outside every contact neighborhood.

Rational simplex vectors give the entropy supremum face by face at infinity. Dini on [-B,infinity]^r and rationally rounded constants yield h_epsilon between chi-epsilon and chi; h_{4^-j}+2*4^-j decreases uniformly to chi. For countable k choose rational gamma_j with gamma_j rho_j<=2^-j(v+1). Upper partial sums plus tail 2^-N(v+1) decrease. Rational local PL approximants with errors epsilon_N=4^-N become decreasing after adding 2sum_{m>=N}epsilon_m. A real logarithmic support C+sum alpha_i log|h_i| on log|h_i|<=B_i has rational PL approximants max(q_m+sum alpha_i,m(log|h_i|-B_i),-m), where rational alpha_i,m increase to alpha_i>0 and rational q_m decrease to C+sum alpha_i B_i. These decrease even at zeros. Add the remainder-series sequence on each common exhaustion neighborhood.

The resulting support is finite at its contact point and has upper FS growth. Subtract a larger ample FS potential, truncate, and use the growth collar to glue the already-PL approximants into genuine global model psh functions. Decreasing closure and the complete-system affine correspondence give actual global affine FS regularization, checking rational coefficients/constants, floors, generators and the infinite series. This uses no singular EP and does not prove norm theorem 6.12.

notes.summary: Wu 6.12 still applies smooth affine regularization over H(s), which can be nondiscrete inside the retained projective unibranch domain. A cusp-product example proves the uncovered hypothesis; it does not disprove the intended theorem.
notes.detailedSummary: A finite degree-two cusp-product map to A3 over trivially valued Qbar, with an analytic branch-plane point having monomial weights 1 and sqrt(2), produces nondiscrete H(s). The normalized preimage of a line through its rational lift is A1 over H(s), exactly the smooth curve used by Wu 6.12 Step 3. Proposition 4.19 and n2's repair retain trivial/discrete field hypotheses. Proposition 6.11 allows arbitrary fields but needs the missing already-regularizable input. Neither the inspected CLD statements nor Wu 6.13 supplies that affine FS regularization. The gap propagates through singular induction and the countable envelope base.
notes.text:
Concrete unresolved application, independently witnessed. Wu2609.27610v1 Proposition 6.12 sets F=H(s) for arbitrary s in an affine-space target at LF2236–2256. At LF2331–2334 it claims affine FS regularizability on the normalized preimage curve because it is smooth, invoking Proposition 4.19. That proposition requires a discrete or trivial valuation; n2's repair does not remove this antecedent.

Let k=Qbar trivially valued, Y=Spec k[a,b,y,z]/(b^2-a^3), S=Spec k[a,y,z], and pi the evident map. Its algebra is free with basis 1,b over k[a,y,z], hence finite flat of degree two. It is étale off a=0, where b and 2b are invertible. Y is an affine chart of the retained projective geometrically unibranch threefold C_cusp times P1 times P1, with normalization P1 cubed and ample exterior-product polarization. The cusp normalization has singleton geometric fibers with unchanged residue fields; its product preserves this universal-homeomorphism property.

Choose s with kernel (a), v(y)=1, v(z)=sqrt(2), and a polynomial in y,z valued by its least monomial weight. Distinct monomials have distinct weights, so this is multiplicative. H(s) is the completion of k(y,z) and contains values m+n sqrt(2), for integers m,n. The pigeonhole principle for fractional parts of j sqrt(2) gives nonzero such values arbitrarily close to zero. Its valuation is nontrivial and nondiscrete; completion preserves these elements and values.

The F-rational lift has coordinates (0,y_s,z_s). The line a=tau, y=y_s, z=z_s is generically étale. Its preimage b^2=tau^3 normalizes to A1_F with tau=t^2 and b=t^3. Thus the precise smooth-curve application occurs over an uncovered field internally in the assigned projective domain. This is an algebraic proof, not a numerical search or a counterexample to the intended norm/envelope theorem.

Wu 6.11 permits every complete field, but its input must already have decreasing affine FS regularization. It cannot establish the missing input in 6.12. Wu 6.13 gives a boundary-limit assertion at a closed point of a smooth curve, not affine regularization. The inspected CLD statements establish current/model positivity and model-measure compatibility, not the required curve FS approximation. A possible repair is independent arbitrary-H(s) curve regularization, or a local-psh norm/boundary-limit proof checking multiplicities and exact local definitions. Neither is proved here.

This gap remains in 6.12(2), then 6.15 Step 5 and 6.14, singular-stratum induction 6.3, weak/global identification 6.5, and the countable-field proof of body 7.1. The n2 supporting construction does not supply the norm antecedent. Cardinality and real-class removal remain conditional on a proved countable rational envelope case. This is a concrete application failure, not a bibliographic or preprint-status objection.

notes.text:
Exact disposition: the original target is unchanged and remains unproved. n1 supplies the genuine mixed finite-energy operator, raw mass V, probability normalization, E(phi+c)=E(phi)+c, necessary finite-dual-energy targets and one-constant uniqueness/comparison. The global construction also covers ample real numerical Cartier classes. Arbitrary-support existence, compactness/completeness and onto normalization remain conditional on actual EP. n2 repairs smooth affine regularization and the actual FS supporting replacement. n3 leaves the specific H(s) norm application unresolved. No unrelated valuation, characteristic, nonample, nonprojective or analytic axis is inferred.

Cardinality removal has its antecedent visible. Finite geometry, polarization, obstacle and model competitor data descend to countable algebraically closed subfields. Regular characteristic-zero extensions preserve normalization, geometric branches, vertical R1/S2 and relative integral closure in the given generic fiber. Vertical components remain geometrically integral; unchanged multiplicities, divisorial restrictions and intersection degrees yield genuine mixed-measure pushforward, extended by decreasing approximation. If the countable envelope u1=P(f1) exists continuously, the same envelope for u1+t(f1-u1) yields genuine contact orthogonality. Positivity and pushforward put the pulled-back measure on contact; BJ global domination controls the global model competitor on the singular variety. Model suprema and PL density remove cardinality. Rational ample classes approaching a real class from above and actual PSH class closure remove rationality. These implications do not establish the missing countable base.

For geometrically unibranch X, normalization q is finite birational degree one and a universal homeomorphism with unchanged residue fields in characteristic zero; analytification is a homeomorphism. One-way psh pullback, equal volume, E(q*phi)=E(phi), and genuine mixed-measure pushforward are unconditional. Onto psh descent separately requires BJ Lemma 5.13's larger classes with EP, through logarithmic-ideal corrections and increasing-limit removal. Onto E1 and equal dual energies are not asserted here.

The nodal obstruction is unconditional. On a rational projective nodal curve, let p1,p2 be distinct node preimages in P1, d=deg L>0 and v=ord_p1. The downstairs delta_v has finite dual energy. Blow up P1 times A1 at (p1,0); p*(q*L)+d X0-d E has central degrees 0,d and multiplicities one. It is relatively nef and its genuine raw model measure is d delta_v. Its potential is d max(1-s,0) on the p1 ray and d elsewhere, giving endpoint values 0,d. A downstairs E1 solution would pull to the same target upstairs by genuine pushforward, positivity, fixed mass and the singleton lift of v. Upstairs uniqueness forces this potential plus a constant, whereas any downstairs pullback has equal endpoint values at the two points mapping to the node. Contradiction: an actual finite-energy target is nonsolvable outside the unibranch domain.
